result.summary: This agreement is a merger transaction involving Five Prime Therapeutics, Inc. The document details extensive representations and warranties concerning intellectual property rights, data protection, and termination provisions. The contract includes significant protections for intellectual property and specific termination fees.

R-TERM-01 Partial: Termination provisions exist for breach, but convenience termination for customers is absent.

agentPerspectives.roleDescription: Represents the counterparty's interests in securing robust deal certainty and high termination penalties.
agentPerspectives.stance: Aggressive on deal protection and securing large termination fees.
keyPoints: Insists on a substantial $76 million termination fee.
Protects proprietary IP ownership through strict assignment clauses.
agentPerspectives.counterOfferRecommendation: Negotiate a lower termination fee threshold and mutual termination rights.

agentPerspectives.roleDescription: Focuses on closing the transaction efficiently while ensuring core operational continuity.
agentPerspectives.stance: Pragmatic compromise to finalize the merger without undue friction.
keyPoints: Prioritizes clear closing conditions and seamless transfer of assets.
agentPerspectives.counterOfferRecommendation: Streamline closing conditions and maintain clear escrow terms.

agentPerspectives.roleDescription: Evaluates agreement terms against enterprise buyer risk tolerances and playbook rules.
agentPerspectives.stance: Cautious regarding missing liability caps and unaddressed indemnification.
keyPoints: Identified total absence of standard vendor indemnification provisions.
Noted missing liability limitation caps in the provided excerpts.
agentPerspectives.counterOfferRecommendation: Insert comprehensive vendor IP indemnification and a standard liability cap.

redlines.originalText: In the event that Parent or its designee shall receive full payment pursuant to this Section 9.3(b), the receipt of the Termination Fee shall be deemed to be liquidated damages for any and all losses or damages suffered or incurred by Parent
redlines.proposedText: In the event that Parent or its designee shall receive full payment pursuant to this Section 9.3(b), the receipt of the Termination Fee shall be deemed to be liquidated damages, and the Company shall retain a right to terminate for convenience upon thirty (30) days written notice.

chainOfThought.opposingCounselStance: Parent will argue that the termination fee provides certainty and is standard for merger and acquisition transactions of this scale.
chainOfThought.commercialRiskAssessment: Locks the company into the transaction without an exit option for convenience, exposing it to significant downside risk.
chainOfThought.legalRationale: Aligns the agreement with enterprise standards by allowing a termination for convenience option.
chainOfThought.negotiationTalkingPoint: We need a standard 30-day termination for convenience option to manage ongoing commercial viability. Fallback: 60 days notice with no cancellation penalties.

redlines.originalText: Section 4.8(d) of the Company Disclosure Schedule sets forth each license agreement pursuant to which the Company has a license or other right to any material Intellectual Property Right
redlines.proposedText: Section 4.8(d) of the Company Disclosure Schedule sets forth each license agreement, ensuring that all custom deliverables and customer data remain sole property of Customer as Work Made for Hire.

chainOfThought.opposingCounselStance: The drafting party will maintain that existing disclosure schedules adequately capture all necessary intellectual property rights without needing broader representations.
chainOfThought.commercialRiskAssessment: Relying solely on disclosure schedules risks vendor control over core intellectual property and custom work products.
chainOfThought.legalRationale: Protects customer work product ownership and ensures clarity on licensing rights.
chainOfThought.negotiationTalkingPoint: We require explicit confirmation that customer data and custom deliverables remain our property. Fallback: Vendor retains background IP and grants a perpetual irrevocable license.

redlines.originalText: Indemnified Persons is defined in Section 7.4(a) of this Agreement. Indemnifying Parties is defined in Section 7.4(b) of this Agreement.
redlines.proposedText: Each party shall mutually indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the other party against third-party IP infringement, data breaches, and gross negligence.

chainOfThought.opposingCounselStance: The drafting party will point out that indemnification terms are addressed elsewhere or handled through general transaction covenants.
chainOfThought.commercialRiskAssessment: Leaves the company completely unprotected against third-party IP infringement claims and data breaches.
chainOfThought.legalRationale: Establishes a balanced, mutual indemnification framework required by enterprise risk policies.
chainOfThought.negotiationTalkingPoint: A mutual indemnity for third-party claims is standard market practice. Fallback: Mutual indemnification with standard exclusions for customer materials.

redlines.originalText: The Company has taken commercially reasonable actions to protect the security and integrity of the Company Systems, including taking and storing on-site and off-site of back-up copies of material data and information.
redlines.proposedText: The Company has taken commercially reasonable actions and shall notify Customer of any security breach within twenty-four (24) to forty-eight (48) hours, complying with strict security standards.

chainOfThought.opposingCounselStance: The drafting party will argue that a commercially reasonable standard is standard practice for system security and avoids strict liability or impractical notice windows.
chainOfThought.commercialRiskAssessment: Vague security standards and lack of mandatory breach notification windows expose the buyer to unmitigated data loss risks.
chainOfThought.legalRationale: Enforces a strict 24-48 hour breach notification timeline to satisfy enterprise data privacy requirements.
chainOfThought.negotiationTalkingPoint: We require rapid visibility into security incidents to comply with regulatory obligations. Fallback: Breach notice within 72 hours without unreasonable delay.

obligations.requirement: The Company shall promptly notify Parent of any Legal Proceeding commenced against the Company or its directors relating to the Transactions.
The Company shall pay to Parent the Termination Fee by wire transfer of same day funds under specified termination conditions.
obligations.triggerOrDeadline: Upon termination of the agreement under specific conditions
obligations.breachConsequence: Liquidated damages and waiver of other claims

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: Indemnified Persons is defined in Section 7.4(a) of this Agreement. Indemnifying Parties is defined in Section 7.4(b) of this Agreement.
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: (a) Provider Indemnification. Provider shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer... (b) Customer Indemnification. Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Provider... (c) Procedure.
deviations: The provided excerpts lack full mutual indemnification mechanics and defense procedures.
missingProtections: Explicit third-party IP infringement defense and hold-harmless obligations.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Review the full text of Section 7.4 to ensure comprehensive indemnification protections are present.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: This Agreement shall be governed by, and construed in accordance with, the Laws of the State of Delaware... Each of the Parties irrevocably and unconditionally consents and submits to the exclusive jurisdiction and venue of the Court of Chancery of the State of Delaware.
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardTitle: Clear Governing Law and Neutral Forum
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: This Agreement is governed by the laws of [agreed jurisdiction], without regard to its conflict-of-laws rules. Each party submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts located in [agreed neutral venue]...
deviations: Specifies Delaware state courts and Court of Chancery instead of generic neutral forum placeholders.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: The governing law and forum selection clauses are robust and properly aligned with standard Delaware corporate practice.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: collection, storage, sharing, transfer, disposition, protection, processing or other use of any Personally Identifiable Information, or violation of any Data Privacy and Security Requirements.
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardTitle: SOC 2 Type II Security Covenants & 48-Hour Security Breach Notification
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: (a) Security Measures. Provider shall maintain administrative, physical, and technical safeguards... (b) Security Incident Notification... (c) Data Return & Destruction.
deviations: Excerpts focus on representations regarding past compliance rather than ongoing affirmative security covenants and 48-hour breach notification.
missingProtections: Explicit SOC 2 certification requirements and 48-hour incident notification timelines.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Verify if operational data security covenants and specific breach notification timelines are detailed elsewhere in the agreement schedules.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: if to Parent or Purchaser: Amgen Inc. One Amgen Center Drive Thousand Oaks, California... if to the Company: Five Prime Therapeutics, Inc. 111 Oyster Point Boulevard South San Francisco, CA...
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: All notices under this Agreement must be in writing and delivered by hand, by recognised courier, or by email with confirmation of receipt, to the addresses stated in the order form...
deviations: Specific physical addresses and fax numbers are provided directly in the text rather than referencing an order form.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Ensure contact details and delivery methods remain accurate for all parties.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: No Company Associate or other Person... owns or has any claim, right or interest to or in any Owned Company IP and each Company Associate... has signed a written agreement containing a present assignment to the Company...
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardTitle: Each Party Keeps Its Pre-Existing IP; Licence to Deliverables
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: Each party retains all rights in its intellectual property existing before or developed independently of this Agreement. The Customer owns all deliverables created specifically for it upon payment.
deviations: Language addresses employee IP assignment and company-owned IP representations rather than general commercial pre-existing IP and deliverable licenses.
missingProtections: Explicit license grants for embedded pre-existing materials in custom deliverables.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Ensure commercial IP ownership provisions appropriately reflect the operational context of the engagement.

benchmarkComparisons.contractClauseText: the Company shall pay, or shall cause to be paid, to Parent the Termination Fee by wire transfer of same day funds... As used herein, Termination Fee means a cash amount equal to $76,000,000.
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardTitle: Notice and Exit Right on Change of Control
benchmarkComparisons.goldStandardText: A party undergoing a Change of Control shall notify the other party in writing within thirty (30) days. If the acquiring entity is a competitor... the other party may terminate...
deviations: Excerpts deal with acquisition termination fees and superior offers rather than standard commercial change of control exit rights.
missingProtections: Commercial termination rights upon a change of control involving a competitor.
benchmarkComparisons.recommendation: Review change of control clauses to determine if commercial partnership protections are needed alongside M&A deal terms.

missingProtections.title: Renewal with Reminder and Short Opt-Out Notice
missingProtections.standardText: This Agreement renews for successive twelve (12) month terms unless either party gives written notice of non-renewal at least thirty (30) days before the end of the current term. The Provider shall send a written renewal reminder, including any price change, at least sixty (60) days before each renewal date. Renewal fees may not increase by more than the lower of five percent (5%) or the applicable consumer price index.
missingProtections.evidence: This agreement is a definitive merger transaction rather than a recurring commercial service contract, making automated renewal and price cap provisions inapplicable.

opposingFindings.quote: In the event that Parent or its designee shall receive full payment pursuant to this Section 9.3(b), the receipt of the Termination Fee shall be deemed to be liquidated damages for any and all losses or damages suffered or incurred by Parent
opposingFindings.issue: The agreement includes a substantial termination fee ($76,000,000) treated as liquidated damages, restricting the company from recovering additional actual damages while failing to provide a customer termination for convenience right.
opposingFindings.leverage: Parent will argue that the termination fee provides certainty and is standard for merger and acquisition transactions of this scale.

opposingFindings.quote: Section 4.8(d) of the Company Disclosure Schedule sets forth each license agreement pursuant to which the Company has a license or other right to any material Intellectual Property Right
opposingFindings.issue: The contract references inbound and outbound licenses via disclosure schedules rather than ensuring robust customer ownership or explicit standard IP protections, risking vendor control over IP.
opposingFindings.leverage: The drafting party will maintain that existing disclosure schedules adequately capture all necessary intellectual property rights without needing broader representations.

opposingFindings.quote: Indemnified Persons is defined in Section 7.4(a) of this Agreement. Indemnifying Parties is defined in Section 7.4(b) of this Agreement.
opposingFindings.issue: The provided excerpts lack explicit mutual indemnification protections for third-party IP infringement or data breaches, leaving potential gaps in risk allocation.
opposingFindings.leverage: The drafting party will point out that indemnification terms are addressed elsewhere or handled through general transaction covenants.

opposingFindings.quote: The Company has taken commercially reasonable actions to protect the security and integrity of the Company Systems, including taking and storing on-site and off-site of back-up copies of material data and information.
opposingFindings.issue: Data security relies merely on 'commercially reasonable actions' without imposing strict breach notification timelines such as 24 to 48 hours.
opposingFindings.leverage: The drafting party will argue that a commercially reasonable standard is standard practice for system security and avoids strict strict liability or impractical notice windows.
